independence_declaration.statement: I (domain-reviewer) authored no implementation in the DG1 candidate. The round-13 repairs were written by backend-workflow-engineer (F-DG1-134, T-DG1-BE14, commit e71f3d0) and delivery-orchestrator (F-DG1-216, the D-055 text, commit 85af2e6). F-DG1-216 was raised by qa-verifier and F-DG1-134 by code-security-reviewer, not by me. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-13 record; I read none of them.

Check HEAD, that the repository is not shallow, and the recomputed candidate ID, both in the repository and in a full disposable clone checked out at the freeze commit 08cbd12. Check that HEAD (ed2160d) differs from the freeze commit only by candidate-excluded metadata.

checks_run.procedure: Verify F-DG1-216. Read D-055 at the freeze commit and pull out every mention of rule 5, residual (a) and enumeration. Count the stale sentence at the round-12 freeze and at the round-13 freeze. Grep the candidate (metadata excluded) for 'residual (a)'. Compare with the testkit header's own statements.
checks_run.command: git show 08cbd12:docs/delivery/decisions.md | grep -c 'reaching it by namespace enumeration is residual (a)'; same at 987ae02; git show 08cbd12:docs/delivery/decisions.md | sed -n 7p | grep -oE '.{0,80}(rule 5|residual \(a\)|enumerat)[^|]{0,160}'; git grep -nE 'residual \(a\)' 08cbd12 -- . ':!docs/delivery/reviews' ':!docs/delivery/test-evidence' ':!docs/delivery/runs' ':!docs/delivery/findings.json' ':!docs/delivery/assignments' ':!docs/delivery/handbacks'; git show 08cbd12:apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts | grep -nE 'closed by rule 5|CLOSED by rule 5|Residual limits'
checks_run.expected: The stale sentence is present at 987ae02 (count 1) and absent at 08cbd12 (count 0). Both D-055 mentions say the node:crypto enumeration route is closed by rule 5 (named imports only), consistent with testkit lines 26 and 67. No remaining candidate text calls that route residual (a).
checks_run.actual: Count 1 at 987ae02 and 0 at 08cbd12. D-055 now says: '…nor, by itself, the runtime-enumeration reach of such a member (F-DG1-132/215) — that route is closed by rule 5 (named-imports-only for node:crypto, F-DG1-133)' and '…since rule 5 (F-DG1-132/133), unreachable by namespace enumeration — a module may import node:crypto through named imports only…'. D-055's residual list keeps only '(a) runtime data-flow', which matches the testkit header ('(a) runtime DATA FLOW over PLAIN OBJECTS…'; 'is CLOSED by rule 5'). The remaining 'residual (a)' hits are architecture.test.ts:544, an accurate historical note ('pinned then as residual (a)' about the round-11 lint), and stages.json (metadata). The decision record no longer contradicts the lint.

checks_run.procedure: Check independently that the F-DG1-134 fix does not change the verdict on the real module tree and does close the evasion, using a reviewer-authored probe. P1: inventory of the real module tree by extension, via readdir rather than walk(). P2: walk() equals the .ts/.tsx inventory. P3: moduleViolations is [] for all 13 declared modules. P4: plant .mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs/.js/.jsx files in the REAL modules/transformations directory of the clone; each must be flagged (rule 5 + deep import), and removal must restore []. P5: non-code files are ignored. P6: declaration files (.d.ts/.d.mts). Control: run the same probe against the round-12 testkit (987ae02).
checks_run.command: cp 02-walk-scope-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom-r13-probe.test.ts; PATH=<node bin>:$PATH node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-dom-r13-probe.test.ts --reporter=verbose; rm the probe; control: git show 987ae02:apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts > zz-old.testkit.ts and the same probe pointed at it (Node 22)
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 08cbd12; Node v22.22.2 and v24.21.0
checks_run.expected: Real tree: 41 .ts files, 0 others, walk() unchanged, 13/13 modules with zero violations. Every planted code extension is flagged with the fix and missed by the round-12 lint. Non-code files are ignored.
checks_run.actual: 13/13 probe tests pass on both runtimes. Inventory {".ts":41}; walk() returns the same 41 files; modules platform…admin (13) all []. Each of .mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs/.js/.jsx gives 2 violations (node:crypto namespace binding plus 'only access/index.ts is public'), and [] after removal. .json/.md/.sql/.mts.map are ignored. Control against the round-12 testkit: all six P4 cases FAIL (0 violations, the original evasion reproduces), while P1–P3 and P5 pass. Observation (P6, not a finding): a declaration file (.d.ts or .d.mts) makes moduleViolations throw ('Debug Failure. Output generation failed' from ts.transpileModule in syntaxErrors). The lint fails CLOSED (the architecture suite would go red) and does not pass the file silently. For .d.ts this is identical on the round-12 lint, so it is pre-existing; for .d.mts the round-12 lint skipped the file silently, so the fix makes it fail closed.

summary: PASS on candidate sha256:00f1498c…c80b (freeze 08cbd12). F-DG1-216 verified and CLOSED_VERIFIED: D-055 now says the node:crypto enumeration route is closed by rule 5, consistent with the testkit. The F-DG1-134 fix leaves the real module tree's verdict unchanged (41 .ts files, 0 others, all 13 modules with zero violations) and closes the extension evasion: planted .mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs/.js/.jsx files are flagged, whereas the round-12 lint misses them. The round-13 code diff is test-only (testkit and test). Product, contract, data model, ADR and i18n diffs are empty. Unit tests 320/320 and architecture tests 127/127 on Node 22 and 24, integration 200/200 on both, live scenario 108/108 with ar/en screens inspected, static checks green, register consistent. No new findings and no open Critical/High/mandatory finding. One observation, not raised as a finding: declaration files make the lint throw, so it fails closed; this was pre-existing for .d.ts.
